title: A Spring Cleaning Shelf
description: Find familiar household words for cleaning objects, small containers, and tidying actions.
cardDescription: Find familiar household words for cleaning objects, small containers, and tidying actions.
focus: The clues identify supplies by their purpose. Some answers name a tool, while others name an ordinary action.
solvingTip: Look for something that wipes, sweeps, holds, or arranges.
words: Long-handled tool used to wash a floor
Bristled tool used to sweep loose dirt
Piece of fabric used for wiping a surface
Tool with bristles for loosening dirt
Soft tool used to remove loose surface dust
Porous absorbent object used for wiping
Cleaning substance that can form a lather in water
Liquid used to rinse household surfaces
To wash away remaining soap with clean liquid
To rub a surface to improve its shine
To put household items into groups
To expose a room or fabric to fresh moving atmosphere

answerNotes.DUSTER: A duster removes loose dust. It is separate from the container holding water for washing.
answerNotes.SPONGE: A sponge is absorbent and porous. The clue identifies the wiping object rather than a named fabric.
answerNotes.RINSE: Rinsing removes remaining cleaning material. The word names an action rather than a product.
answerNotes.POLISH: Polish is a verb about improving shine here. It does not name a nationality in this clue.

title: Opening the Garden Gate
description: Walk into a spring garden through familiar entrance features, supports, and path materials.
cardDescription: Walk into a spring garden through familiar entrance features, supports, and path materials.
focus: The clues describe the structures around a garden boundary. Position and purpose distinguish the small parts.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a movable part, a support, or a route feature.
words: Movable entrance panel in a garden fence
Small fastening holding a gate shut
Jointed hardware allowing a gate to swing
Upright support for a fence or gate
Walking route leading from a garden entrance
Narrow planted area along a garden’s edge
Curved overhead structure above a path
Row of shrubs forming a garden boundary
Small stones spread on a garden path
Long outdoor seat placed beside a path
Raised level climbed at a garden entrance

answerNotes.LATCH: A latch holds the gate closed. A hinge allows it to move, so the two pieces have different jobs.
answerNotes.TRELLIS: A trellis is an open support for plants. It differs from a solid fence panel.
answerNotes.BED: Bed is a planting area here. The clue does not mean furniture for sleeping.
answerNotes.HEDGE: A hedge is formed from growing plants. Its material distinguishes it from a built fence.

title: The Umbrella Stand
description: Look over a familiar spring umbrella through its parts, shapes, and the objects around an entrance.
cardDescription: Look over a familiar spring umbrella through its parts, shapes, and the objects around an entrance.
focus: The clues focus on the umbrella as an everyday object. A whole canopy and the smaller supports beneath it have distinct names.
solvingTip: Look for an outer covering, a supporting part, or a place for storing the item.
words: Handheld canopy opened to keep off spring rain
Fabric covering spread above an umbrella’s frame
Slender support holding an umbrella’s fabric open
Central long support of an umbrella
Part grasped while holding an umbrella
Small outer end of an umbrella rib
Band holding a folded umbrella closed
To close fabric into a compact arrangement
Holder where umbrellas are placed near a door
Curved support used to hang an umbrella
Small drop of water falling from a wet object
Covered with moisture after a shower
Movable entrance beside an umbrella holder
Floor covering that may catch water near an entrance

answerNotes.CANOPY: The canopy is the fabric shelter. The ribs are the supports beneath it.
answerNotes.SHAFT: The shaft is the umbrella’s central support. It differs from the shorter ribs spreading outward.
answerNotes.RIB: Rib names a structural support in this clue. It does not refer to a bone in the body.
answerNotes.STAND: Stand is a storage holder here. The clue asks for an object rather than the action of rising.

title: A Backyard Nest Box
description: Explore a spring birdhouse through familiar building parts and nesting words.
cardDescription: Explore a spring birdhouse through familiar building parts and nesting words.
focus: The clues combine a small outdoor structure with the animals and materials around it. Direct definitions distinguish the house from its contents.
solvingTip: Check whether a clue asks for a building part, a nest material, or a bird feature.
words: Small built shelter intended for nesting birds
Round entrance opening in a nest box
Upright side of a small built shelter
Structure holding a bird’s eggs or young
Small woody piece used in some nests
Narrow plant blades used as nest material by some birds
Light body covering sometimes found near a nest
Small songbird that may use a nest box
Young bird newly hatched from an egg
Shell-covered structure from which a chick develops
Hard mouthpart used by a bird
Resting support near a bird’s shelter

answerNotes.BIRDHOUSE: Birdhouse names the built shelter. The nest is the structure a bird may place inside or elsewhere.
answerNotes.TWIG: A twig is a small woody branch. It is one possible nest material rather than a whole nest.
answerNotes.CHICK: Chick names a young bird. The clue does not require one particular species.
answerNotes.PERCH: A perch is a resting support. It does not refer to a fish in this birdhouse context.

title: A Park Bench in Spring
description: Take a park visit through familiar water birds, flowering growth, and places to walk or sit.
cardDescription: Take a park visit through familiar water birds, flowering growth, and places to walk or sit.
focus: The clues describe a small outdoor scene. Living things and built objects offer different ways into the grid.
solvingTip: Look for a plant, a bird, a place, or a gentle movement.
words: Public outdoor area with paths and places to sit
Long seat placed beside a park path
Route followed by walkers through a park
Small body of still water in a park
Water bird commonly seen swimming on a park pond
Tall waterside plant with a slender stem
Tree often associated with flexible branches beside water
Unopened plant growth seen on spring branches
Flower appearing on a spring tree
Structure carrying a path over a stream
Shelter from direct sunlight beneath a tree
To walk in an unhurried way

answerNotes.BLOSSOM: Blossom names a flower here. It can also be a verb meaning develop or come into flower.
answerNotes.REED: Reed names a plant in this clue. It does not mean the vibrating part of a wind instrument.
answerNotes.WILLOW: Willows are familiar waterside trees with flexible branches. The clue uses that association rather than one leaf color.
answerNotes.STROLL: A stroll is an unhurried walk. The clue asks for the action rather than the route called a path.
